analysis.title: HubSpot Inc. (HUBS) 3Q26: Headwinds persist as AI reshapes the buying motion
key_insights: HUBS was indicated down about 9% after hours on 3Q26 results. Revenue was 2% above the Street, billings and gross margin were in line, and EBIT margin was about 200bps above (FactSet).
Net revenue retention (NRR) was 101%, down 1pp quarter on quarter.
4Q revenue guidance was 2% below the Street at the midpoint and EBIT margin was guided 100bps below.

GS attributes the weaker fundamentals to worsening headwinds from AI-driven buying behavior and budget sensitivity. These became more pronounced in 3Q and are expected to persist through 4Q and into 2027, driving continued deceleration.

Customers are increasingly experimenting before committing spend. HubSpot has responded with free trials and pricing tied more closely to value and outcomes. Agent trials grew 64% qoq in 3Q, but this is extending buying cycles and requires more hands-on support from partners and solution consultants.

Budget sensitivity is rising. Inbound demand is under pressure as discovery shifts toward intent-based marketing, LLM connectors and AEO. Upmarket deals have larger buying committees and longer sales cycles, and downmarket customers are more price sensitive.

HubSpot is engaging more stakeholders earlier. Win rates are nearly 3x higher in deals with 5+ buying committee members when multiple stakeholders are engaged, and close rates are higher on larger deals with C-suite involvement.
GS believes HubSpot is taking the right long-term actions. The key for the stock is showing that these changes translate into greater customer value and differentiation versus competitors.

The 12-month price target stays at $276 (Buy). The fundamental value multiple was cut to 10x EV/FCF from 12x on lower growth expectations, and the M&A value is set at 20x EV/FCF, the bottom quintile of prior transactions, given the ongoing AI overhang.
GS cut 2027 and 2028 revenue forecasts to $4,063mn and $4,411mn from $4,133mn and $4,546mn, and raised 2027 and 2028 EPS to $17.49 and $21.49 from $16.03 and $18.96.
At $216.64 the stock offers 27.4% upside to the target. The stock is down 54.1% over 12 months and 59.6% relative to the S&P 500.

market_movers.rationale: Buy rating held since Dec 13, 2021 and price target unchanged at $276 despite a guide below the Street. Valuation multiple was lowered to reflect slower growth and the AI overhang.

sector_views.rationale: AI is changing software buying behavior toward trials, outcome-based pricing and larger buying committees, which lengthens sales cycles. The report frames this as an ongoing overhang on growth expectations.

earnings_insights: 3Q26 reported total revenue $948mn vs GSe $925mn and Street $926mn (FactSet), +17% yoy, 2.4% above the Street.
3Q26 reported subscription revenue $930mn vs GSe $904mn and Street $906mn, +18% yoy. Professional services revenue $17mn vs GSe $21mn and Street $18mn.
3Q26 reported operating income $214mn vs GSe $188mn and Street $188mn, a 23% margin and +33% yoy.
3Q26 reported EPS $3.81 vs GSe $3.27 and Street $3.27, +43% yoy. The report does not state whether the figure is GAAP or adjusted.
3Q26 reported billings $925mn vs GSe $918mn and Street $923mn, +15% yoy. Free cash flow $188mn vs GSe $184mn and Street $187mn, a 20% margin.
4Q26 guidance (company): revenue 2% below the Street at the midpoint, EBIT margin 100bps below the Street.
GS estimates (forecast): revenue $3,686mn for 2026, $4,063mn for 2027 and $4,411mn for 2028. EPS $13.52, $17.49 and $21.49. Revenue growth 17.7%, 10.2% and 8.6%.
GS quarterly EPS estimates (forecast): $3.78 for 12/26E, $3.86 for 3/27E and $4.30 for 6/27E.
risk_factors: Tighter lending standards could have an outsized negative impact on access to funding for SMBs.
Inability to expand beyond core hubs.
AI-driven shifts in buying behavior and discovery could lengthen sales cycles and pressure inbound demand through 2027.
